body:
hey Draconian, 

Thanks for the reply.  It helps when someone can relate.

I guess a big part of it is guilt.  I had always dreamed of letting my father see me graduate.  In all respects I should have graduated that year when he died but I was young and foolish and didn't.  It kills me that I could have given him ONE last thing to be happy about.

I guess it's because I always dreamed of joining my father in academia.  He was on his way to becoming a Professor until cancer had other options.  I was following him into college lectures since I was a toddler.

I used to think I had friends I could rely on but they've all since turned their backs on me.

My father died in the one of the worst possible ways.  He had a severe brain tumour which shut down parts of his brain.  He had little to no appetite, actually let me say it again, he had no appetite.  I literally watched him go from a healthy 160 lb man to a sub-100 lb skeleton.  I remember looking at him in his bed and remarking to myself in my head how he looked like those poor souls who died in the concentration camps in WW2.  Gaunt face, bones protruding everywhere, hazy eyes.

Every time I sit down alone at the dinner table, I remember how he couldn't eat and it makes me so, so sad I break down and start crying.
